subject: mathematics
question_text: In △ABC, prove that tan(A/2) + tan(B/2) + tan(C/2) = (bc + ca + ab − s²)/Δ.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.122, chapter 12 PROPERTIES OF TRIANGLES, Very Short Answer question 5(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write each tangent over Δ
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. tan(A/2) = (s−b)(s−c)/Δ: the two factors are the ones that do NOT carry the letter a.
steps.memory_tip: For tan(A/2) the numerator is (s−b)(s−c) — the two factors that do not carry the letter a.

recall.must_convey: That tan(A/2) = (s−b)(s−c)/Δ, and the same pattern gives the other two tangents.
accept: tan half A is s minus b into s minus c over delta
rationalise the half angle root so the bottom becomes Heron's product which is delta
the numerator uses the two brackets that do not contain a
tan half A ki s minus b into s minus c by delta vasthundi
write all three tangents over the same delta

steps.why: Multiplying the top and the bottom of the half-angle root by (s−b)(s−c) makes the denominator Heron's product, which is Δ. All three tangents then share one denominator.
common_mistakes: Writing tan(A/2) = s(s−a)/Δ, which is cot(A/2).

steps.label: Expand the three products
steps.margin_note: No separate mark at this length. Each bracket pair gives s², a term in s, and a product of two sides.
steps.memory_tip: Every product has the same shape: s² − s(sum of the two sides) + (their product).

recall.must_convey: That each product expands to s² − s(sum of two sides) + (product of those two sides).
accept: expand each pair to s squared minus s times the sum plus the product
all three expansions have the same shape
write out s minus b into s minus c as s squared minus s b plus c plus b c
prathi jodi ni expand chesthe s square minus s into sum plus product vasthundi
expand the three brackets before adding

steps.why: Each product expands to the same shape: an s², a term in s, and a product of two sides. Writing all three out makes the collection in the next step a single addition.
common_mistakes: Dropping one of the three products.

steps.label: Collect and conclude
steps.margin_note: The other mark. a + b + c = 2s turns 3s² − 2s(2s) into −s², which is the sign the answer needs.

recall.must_convey: That a+b+c = 2s makes the s-terms 4s², leaving ab + bc + ca − s² over Δ.
accept: add the three expansions and use a plus b plus c equals two s
three s squared minus four s squared leaves minus s squared
the answer is a b plus b c plus c a minus s squared over delta
a plus b plus c ante two s, so three s square minus four s square
collect the terms and the s squared becomes negative

steps.why: Each side appears in exactly two of the three products, so the terms in s add to 2s(a+b+c). Replacing a+b+c by 2s is what turns 3s² into −s².
common_mistakes: Writing a + b + c = s instead of 2s.
